_comment: Build Log — living per-project documentation. Edit as each project is built; the panel (panels/build_log.html) re-renders from this file. Schema per project: id, name, week, status(done|in_progress|planned|slipped), headline, metrics[{label,value}], entries[{date,title,status,detail,refs[{label,kind(commit|file|run|link),href}]}], decisions[{title,detail}]. Newest entries first.

projects.name: Music Genre — BEARDOWN
projects.headline: Genre family mk1→mk2→mk2.5 locked. mk2 (RRM-swept, cfg 17) deploys at VAL 0.793 / TEST 0.760 — beats mk1 by +6 test. mk2.5 falsified the reliability metric honestly: RRM does not predict held-out rank on a frozen-det head (ρ=−0.00 vs accuracy ρ=0.69). mk3 (3-sec, ×10 data) is next.

entries.title: mk2.5 metric validation — RRM falsified, honestly (the finding)
entries.detail: Firewalled study: refit all 20 configs on full-train, recorded test (selection stayed CV-only). Spearman rank-agreement with TEST accuracy — CV accuracy +0.685, but RRM_w −0.002, equal-weight RRM −0.022, fold-stability −0.008, epistemic U −0.028: every reliability axis is noise as a test-rank predictor. Mechanism: post-hoc LLLA on a frozen DET head gives a near-constant U (0.0258–0.0343), and s is test-uncorrelated. A precise negative result — refines, not refutes, INFO 510 (their RRM used TRAINED Bayesian heads where U varied). Boundary condition: RRM earns its keep only when the reliability axes are both variable AND test-predictive.

entries.title: mk2.5 — Dirichlet / variance re-selection lens (no new model)
entries.detail: Generalized RRM to a simplex weighting: RRM_w = 1−√(Σ wᵢ vᵢ²), w∈Δ²; the locked equal-weight metric is the centroid. Variance-derived w=(0.008,0.926,0.067) zeroes the uninformative U axis on principle → selects cfg 17. Dirichlet sweep (200k uniform-simplex draws): cfg 17 49.5%, cfg 12 48.2%, rest <2% — two robust contenders, choice is weighting-dependent (the only region favoring cfg 12 weights the flat U axis). A selection LENS over sweep.json — no model, no bundle, no FORGE/attribution impact.

entries.title: mk2 locked = cfg 17 — first acceptance PASS, beats mk1 +6 test
entries.detail: Deployed the variance-weighted RRM_w winner: cfg 17 (img768 / tab256 / concat / adam / lr 2.4e-4 / do 0.21,0.17 / ep75, φ-dim 768). Refit on full-train → VAL 0.793 / TEST 0.760 / test macro-F1 0.760, first acceptance PASS (val≥0.75) and clears the paper's 0.766 val band. The macro-F1 jump (0.686→0.760) is on the WEAK genres — a better-balanced classifier, not a luckier one. Equal-weight RRM's nominal winner was cfg 12 (kept as documented contrast); cfg 12 wins ONLY on the flat U axis, so it loses once U is correctly down-weighted. Round-trip OK, max|Δ|=0 — FORGE wraps it unchanged.

entries.title: mk2 sweep — 20-config RRM-selected reliability sweep
entries.detail: Built sweep.py (reuses train.py + llla.py): 20 configs × 3-fold GroupKFold-by-track, each scored on a 4-axis catalogue (accuracy A, fold-σ s, LLLA epistemic U at shared-α τ, off-diagonal rate) + RAM / Pareto / Pearson / dCor. The Bayesian layer is post-hoc LLLA over the frozen det head — the SAME object FORGE serves (selection-U == display-U). Ran clean on CPU (~54 min); catalogue persisted to sweep.json.

entries.title: Input-feature attribution — specced + verified-amenable
entries.detail: Locked the design (FORGE_input_feature_attribution_SPEC.txt): push LLLA σ back through the frozen backbone, ∂σ/∂x = (∂σ/∂φ)·(∂φ/∂x), to NAME which input feature drives a prediction's epistemic uncertainty — the latent features INFO 510 Table A3 could only rank anonymously. Verified against the live bundle: scaler.json carries all 57 named axes + mean/std, arch.json+weights.pt rebuild the frozen backbone — so attribution runs on mk1, cfg 17 and future mk3 with ZERO re-bundling. Ships via precompute-and-cache (mirrors ggn_eig), tabular branch first.

entries.title: Bayesian layer live — LLLA over the frozen head
entries.detail: Last-layer Laplace (closed form from the cached GGN eigenbasis) over the frozen det head: the 0.714 point estimate becomes a decomposable posterior with a live τ-knob. This is the object mk2's RRM selects on AND the object FORGE displays — one llla.py call, two consumers.

entries.title: ML usage / cost estimator built
entries.detail: _shared/usage.py turns every compute.json into energy / carbon / $ with measured-vs-modeled tags, an actual-power hook (RAPL / nvidia-smi), a suite roll-up, and a pre-run projection. Assumptions live in an override YAML for real rates IRL.

entries.title: Song drop-in inference verified (wav + mp3)
entries.detail: End-to-end: drop audio → 30-s windows → clean mel + 57 features → per-genre scores with MC-dropout σ. load_audio hardened (soundfile → librosa fallback → clear error, no silent skip). Works because train + inference now share one mel recipe (validate r=1.0).

entries.title: Backbone frozen: clean-128 / batch-8, CV 0.714
entries.detail: Batch 32→8 lifted CV 0.629→0.714 (+0.086). The frozen deterministic backbone the Bayesian head attaches to. 6× cheaper to train than the original 224 dirty pipeline and the only variant that does real-audio drop-in correctly.

entries.title: Gap diagnosis complete — every cheap hypothesis ruled out
entries.detail: Early stopping, epochs, representation, split, and resolution all tested and eliminated as the cause of the 0.07 gap to 0.766. Lever was batch size; residual is framework (Keras vs PyTorch) + run variance. Faithful, documented reproduction.

entries.title: Clean log-mel regeneration (silent-failure fix)
entries.detail: Kaggle grey PNGs are colormapped matplotlib figures — luminance non-monotonic in mel energy, so a dropped song scored noise. Regenerated all spectrograms from audio with one recipe → train + inference share extract_mel → validate passes by construction.

entries.title: Architecture vetted against the public INFO_510 repo
entries.detail: Confirmed cfg_14: 57 features (length dropped), gated fusion, deterministic head, dense 512/192, lr 7.37e-5, adam, 75 epochs. The winning head was already det — so the FORGE det-backbone + LLLA reproduction is bit-faithful with zero mechanism mismatch.

decisions.title: mk2 = cfg 17, selected by variance-weighted RRM_w (CV-only)
decisions.detail: Deploy the accuracy-strong + stable config; the only metric-region favoring the equal-weight winner (cfg 12) weights the flat, test-uncorrelated U axis. Selection never saw test (firewall).

decisions.title: RRM falsified honestly — the negative result IS the contribution
decisions.detail: On a frozen-det head, neither reliability axis predicts test rank (RRM_w ρ=−0.00, accuracy ρ=+0.69). Built the apparatus to falsify our own metric, ran it, reported it. Refines INFO 510's boundary, doesn't refute it.

decisions.title: Keep BOTH bundles as the result
decisions.detail: beardown_rrm (=cfg 17, deployed) and beardown_rrm_cfg12 (=equal-weight winner). The comparison between them is the mk2.5 finding.

decisions.title: mk3 = beardown_3sec, motivated not guessed
decisions.detail: mk2.5's mechanism (flat U) hands mk3 a hypothesis: does ×10 data (3-sec clips) make U vary again and revive RRM_w's validity? Needs a leakage-safe cutter (track-grouped split).

decisions.title: Batch size was the lever (+0.086 CV)
decisions.detail: 32→8 lifted CV 0.629→0.714. Smaller batch = gradient-noise regularization on small data. Batch 8 is also the BatchNorm floor for this net and matches cfg_14.

decisions.title: 224 resolution ruled out
decisions.detail: Dirty-224 scored CV 0.629 — erased the batch-8 gain at 6× the compute and 3× the memory. Resolution is not the lever.

decisions.title: Clean log-mel over dirty Kaggle grey
decisions.detail: Clean mels score ≥ dirty AND are the only representation reproducible at inference from a dropped wav. A deliberate, documented improvement over the original pipeline.

decisions.title: Split is not the gap
decisions.detail: BEARDOWN's seed-42 stratified split scored ≈ our track split (0.673 vs 0.70) — ruling out an unlucky-draw explanation for the gap.

decisions.title: Freeze, don't chase 0.766
decisions.detail: The wall at ~0.71 is precisely FORGE's motivating example: accuracy-only selection stalls and says nothing about trust. The Bayesian layer is the answer, not more tuning.
